d: Sonia Gandhi speaks about her evolving personal relationship with her mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi. Reflecting on her initial days in the household, she recounts being intimidated by the former Prime Minister and finding it difficult to call her mother because of her attachment to her Italian mother. Describing Indira Gandhi's temper, she says, 'I was in awe of her and a little bit scared too, because once in a while, she lost her temper, and that reminded me of my father, so I used to freeze.'
